newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul's Hyundai Motor resumes Taiwan car exports.
newsitem.headline: Seoul's Hyundai Motor resumes Taiwan car exports.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, South Korea's largest car maker, said on Monday it has resumed exports to Taiwan for the first time since Seoul and Taipei severed diplomatic ties in 1992.
Hyundai Motor said it shipped 270 automobiles on Monday.
Taiwan banned car imports from South Korea after Seoul cut diplomatic ties with Taipei to normalise relations with China in 1992.

Hyundai Motor, a unit of the Hyundai Group, plans to export 2,848 cars to Taiwan this year through its local agent Jack Wang Motor Co, it said. Separately, Hyundai plans to export 5,000 sub-compact cars to the country in 1997 in complete knock-down kits.
"Taiwan looks interested in learning car manufacturing," said Min Kyung-hwan, a Hyundai Motor spokesman.
Hyundai's Excel sub-compact cars would be assembled at Taiwan's Sanfu Motor, a sub-contractor of Jack Wang Motor.
In December, Taiwan agreed to import 7,700 vehicles from South Korea this year.
Kia Motors Corp, South Korea's second-biggest car maker, exported 700 cars to Taiwan last year and planned to ship 1,608 vehicles this year, a Kia spokesman said.
Daewoo Motor Co Ltd, a unit of the Daewoo Group, said it would begin shipping cars to the country from June. Daewoo's export quota to Taiwan was set at 2,344 vehicles.
Ssangyong Motor Co has a quota of 350 and Asia Motors Co will export 300 vehicles.
Hyundai said it had prepared to resume business with Taiwan since Tapei lifted its ban late in 1996.
Hyundai said it was operating 18 showrooms and 30 service centres in Taiwan.
